name: git clone
shortDescription: Clone an existing repository into a new directory. This copies all files, branches, and the complete commit history from a remote source.
detailedDescription:
The `git clone` command creates a full copy of an existing Git repository. Unlike downloading a ZIP, cloning preserves the entire commit history, all branches, and the remote connection. After cloning, you immediately have a working repository with `origin` already configured as the remote.

When you clone, Git performs several operations behind the scenes: it creates a new directory, initializes a `.git` folder inside it, adds a remote called `origin` pointing to the source URL, fetches all branches and tags, and checks out the default branch (usually `main` or `master`) into the working directory.

Git supports multiple protocols for cloning: HTTPS (most common, works through firewalls), SSH (requires key setup, no password prompts), and the Git protocol (fastest but no authentication). Choose based on your setup and security requirements.

parameters.description: The URL or path of the repository to clone. Accepts HTTPS URLs (https://github.com/user/repo.git), SSH URLs (git@github.com:user/repo.git), or local paths (/path/to/repo).
The name of the new directory to clone into. If omitted, Git uses the repository name (e.g., 'repo' from 'repo.git').
Creates a shallow clone with only the last N commits of history. Dramatically reduces download size and time for large repositories. Useful for CI/CD pipelines where you only need the latest code.
Instead of checking out the repository's default branch, check out the specified branch, tag, or commit.
Clone only the history of a single branch (the one specified with --branch, or the default). Reduces clone size when you don't need other branches.
After cloning, initialize and clone all submodules within the repository. Without this, submodule directories will be empty.
Creates a mirror clone — a bare repository that is an exact copy of the remote, including all refs. Used for backup or migration purposes.

examples.title: Basic clone via HTTPS
examples.description: The most common way to clone. Works through firewalls and doesn't require SSH key setup. You'll be prompted for credentials if the repo is private.
examples.code:
git clone https://github.com/facebook/react.git

# This creates a 'react' folder with the full repository

examples.title: Clone via SSH (no password prompts)
examples.description: If you've configured SSH keys with GitHub/GitLab, this method is faster and doesn't require entering credentials. Essential for automated workflows.
examples.code:
git clone git@github.com:facebook/react.git

# Requires SSH key to be added to your GitHub account

examples.title: Shallow clone for CI/CD speed
examples.description: In CI pipelines, you rarely need the full history. A depth of 1 gives you only the latest commit, reducing clone time from minutes to seconds on large repos.
examples.code:
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/torvalds/linux.git

# Linux kernel full clone: ~4.5 GB, 1M+ commits
# Shallow clone (depth 1): ~200 MB, instant

examples.title: Clone a specific branch only
examples.description: When you only need a particular branch, combine --branch and --single-branch to save time and disk space.
examples.code:
git clone --branch develop --single-branch https://github.com/user/repo.git

# Only the 'develop' branch and its history are downloaded

examples.title: Clone into a custom directory name
examples.description: Override the default directory name to something more meaningful for your workflow.
examples.code:
git clone https://github.com/user/api-service.git backend

# Creates a 'backend' folder instead of 'api-service'

commonMistakes.text: If you see `Permission denied (publickey)` when cloning via SSH, your SSH key isn't configured. Either switch to HTTPS or run `ssh-keygen` and add the public key to your Git hosting provider.
Don't clone repositories inside other Git repositories unless you intend to use submodules. Nesting repos causes confusing behavior where the inner repo's changes appear as a single untracked folder.

Shallow clones (`--depth`) cannot push to remotes by default and some Git operations (like `git log` or `git blame`) will show incomplete history. Use `git fetch --unshallow` if you later need the full history.
